title: AA-P10 live retest LR-01 (synthetic sketch written for this retest; not a real study, not a library case, no gold label)
prompt: In a randomized trial, community-dwelling adults aged 70 and older assigned to a home-based balance training program had fewer falls over twelve months than those assigned to general health advice.
context: Researchers randomly assigned community-dwelling adults aged 70 and older (600 in total) either to a home-based balance training program or to general health advice. The program consisted of three short sessions per week. Falls were counted in the same way in both groups. Over twelve months, community-dwelling adults aged 70 and older assigned to the home-based balance training program had 31 percent fewer falls than those assigned to general health advice, and the difference was statistically significant.
